pamphlet_excerpts: Modern Particle Physics: Particle accelerators, sometimes called atom smashers, are machines that can create beams of electrically charged particles and accelerate them (p. 23).
Modern Particle Physics Principle 2: This acceleration increases the particles' energy of motion (p. 23).
Modern Particle Physics Principle 3: Think of the difference between catching a baseball that is gently underhanded to you and catching a fastball fired at youby a major-league pitcher (p. 23).
Modern Particle Physics Principle 4: Energy is the universal container that holdsthings together (p. 23).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (Modern Particle Physics): If you want to break open a container such as an atomor a proton to see what's inside, you must overcome that container'senergy (p. 23).
Step 2 (Modern Particle Physics): From accelerators, scientists get the energy they need to breakopen and explore the makeup of atomic and subatomic particles (p. 23).
Step 3 (Modern Particle Physics): The Large Hadron Collider (LHC) in Geneva, Switzerland, is the world's largest and highest-energy particle accelerator (p. 23).
Step 4 (Modern Particle Physics): Scientists usethe LHC's 17-mile-long underground ring to smash beams of protonsor heavy ions into one another (p. 23).

Discuss the steps taken for the long-term and short-term test methods, tell how to interpret the results, and explain when each type of test should be used. Explain the health concerns related to radon gas and tell what steps can be taken to reduce radon in buildings. (c) Visit a place where X-rays are used. Draw a floor plan of this room. Show where the unit, the unit operator, and the patient would be when the X-ray unit is operated. Step 3 (Nuclear Energy): This was a stack of blocks ofgraphite containing uranium in carefully spaced lumps (p. 53).
Step 4 (Nuclear Energy): Rods of cadmium in the pile soakedup neutrons before they could hit the uranium (p. 53).

pamphlet_excerpts: Careers & Professional Pathways: Nuclear scientists study the structure, properties, and interactions of atomic nuclei and how the elements were formed in the cosmos (p. 78).

Careers & Professional Pathways Principle 2: Experimental nuclear scientists create and analyzeexperiments, while nuclear theorists interpret results fromexperiments and predict new phenomena (p. 78).
Careers & Professional Pathways Principle 3: The ultimate goal isto understand the building blocks of nature and the physicallaws they obey (p. 78).
Careers & Professional Pathways Principle 4: To become a nuclear scientist, most people earn a doctorate in physics or chemistry (p. 78).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (Careers & Professional Pathways): The path to this degree takes manyyears of study and research (p. 78).
Step 2 (Careers & Professional Pathways): As college students majoring inphysics or chemistry, they may take one or two specializednuclear science courses and participate (p. 78).
Step 3 (Careers & Professional Pathways): Then, after graduation from college, they enter a doctoralprogram, taking courses for the first year or two, then beginning full-time research (p. 78).
Step 4 (Careers & Professional Pathways): Almost all nuclear science graduatestudents are paid to go to school through fellowships, teaching assistantships, research assistantships (p. 78).
